_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: a level change of -4 and a slope change of -0.3 a month, AR(1) errors with rho 0.5

agreement.claim: both engines report the same level and slope changes, Newey-West and OLS standard errors
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0. harness/quasi_examples.test.py rebuilds the Newey-West covariance by hand (agreeing to 1e-10) and requires the OLS standard errors to be under 0.8 times the Newey-West ones, with lag-1 residual autocorrelation above 0.2.

recovery.claim: the estimates are close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: A first fixture (60 months, innovation SD 1.5) missed the level by 3.1, close to the effect of 4; the fixture uses 72 months and SD 0.6. Measured by harness/quasi_examples.test.py, running python.py on seeds 0 to 99.

r: NeweyWest(fit, lag = 3, prewhite = FALSE, adjust = FALSE)
